Hi Natalie —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can unblock your integration: 

1) Summary of needs
- SDK setup & auth: you want server-side SDK with short-lived keys for staging and a CI flow for production tokens.
- Embeddings + reranker: pipeline to index customer documents, generate embeddings, then run a reranker on top — you’re seeing intermittent 500s when sending larger batches.
- Structured outputs/tool-calling: low priority for Phase 1.

2) Action items (we’ll own items marked R):
- R: Share current SDK logs and a minimal repro payload (Natalie) — please attach request IDs if available.
- R: Our infra/SEs to review logs and recommend timeout/batching defaults (Dev + Marissa).
- R: If needed, schedule a 1hr debugging session with your platform team this week.

Could you share:
- The staging API key (or grant camila@redwood.com read-only staging access),
- The exact request payload you used (batch size, embedding model, reranker model), and
- Any request IDs around the 5xx windows.

I’m attaching a small integration snippet and would recommend starting with batch_size=32 and request timeout=90s while we triage — will confirm after logs.

Thanks Natalie — I pulled the attached logs. A couple quick hypotheses and repro asks: 

Hypotheses:
- The 5xxs look correlated with very large request payloads (80-100 items). We throttle or OOM some reranker variants when batch plus tokenization expands memory.
- Timeouts: if your client timeout is low, retries pile up and can exacerbate backend pressure.

Immediate recommendations (try in staging):
- Reduce batch_size to 32 per request.
- Increase client timeout to 90s (we default to 60s).
- Add exponential backoff with jitter and limit retries to 3.

Repro steps request: could you run the attached repro script (repro-embed.sh) with the same payload and send back the full X-Request-Id headers for any 5xxs? That will let us trace through the gateway and the reranker host logs.

Also: please grant camila@redwood.com (or dev_patel@redwood.com) a staging API key with the request-logging role so we can inspect traces. If you prefer not to share keys, provide the exact X-Request-Id(s).

Attachment: repro-embed.sh (bash script to reproduce batch request)

Hi all — I dug into the gateway traces for req_abc123 (from your logs) and pulled the following notes:

What I see:
- Gateway received request and forwarded to embeddings host successfully. The embeddings response took ~0.8s per item (expected).
- The reranker stage spikes memory due to tokenization expansion when we batch many long documents. For your finlytics-ranker-v2, we observed an OOM on the host when batch > 48 and average tokenized length > 800. The host then returned 5xx which propagates through the gateway.

Short-term mitigations:
- Set batch_size to 32 for embeddings calls and then run rerank in smaller micro-batches (e.g., groups of 16).
- Increase client timeout to 90s and enable retry-on-5xx with exponential backoff (base 500ms, max 5s).
- Add request-level hedging disabled (we saw hedging amplified load during retries).

Config we recommend for staging (copy/paste):
- client.timeout_ms=90000
- client.batch_size=32
- client.retry.on_5xx=true
- client.retry.max_attempts=3
- reranker.micro_batch_size=16

Longer-term: we can upstream a reranker variant compiled with lower-memory kernels for your model family, or add an automatic splitter in the pipeline. I’ll open a ticket with infra to see if we can auto-fallback to a lower-memory host when we detect tokenization spikes.

Next steps:
- Natalie: can you run repro-embed.sh and share any new X-Request-Id(s)?
- Camila/Dev: we can schedule a 45-min debug session tomorrow 10:00-10:45 PDT — will that work?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
